ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there are 6 identical 1 cm × 1 cm squares; the squares are rotated into a rhombus appearance, arranged along a one-square-wide broken-line/zigzag chain; two adjacent squares touch only along one entire side, no hole is formed, and there is no new square that simultaneously touches extra sides of multiple existing squares. The problem gives that the perimeter of the figure composed of these 6 squares is 14 cm, and asks for the perimeter when the same zigzag shape continues to be extended to 2013 squares. Then reason: In this kind of chain-like extension, each time 1 unit square is added, it shares 1 side with the original figure. This shared side will disappear from the outer perimeter of the original figure, equivalent to subtracting 1 cm; the other 3 sides of the new square become the outer perimeter, equivalent to adding 3 cm, so the net increase of the perimeter is 3 - 1 = 2 cm. From 6 squares increasing to 2013 squares, it is necessary to add 2013 - 6 = 2007 squares. Therefore the new perimeter is 14 + 2 × 2007 = 14 + 4014 = 4028 cm.

method.method_draft: Use an incremental perimeter-growth argument. First read the diagram as a one-square-wide zigzag chain of six unit squares, where each new square in the chain touches the previous shape along exactly one full side and creates no holes or extra contacts. Read from the text that the six-square shape has perimeter 14 cm and that the same zigzag is continued to 2013 squares. The key bridge is: adding one unit square that shares exactly one side removes the shared side from the old outside boundary and contributes the other three sides, so the net perimeter increase is 3 - 1 = 2 cm. There are 2013 - 6 added squares, so compute 14 + 2(2013 - 6) = 4028 cm.

method.method_draft: Use a general adjacency-count formula for a chain of unit squares. From the image, identify that the zigzag is a connected chain of squares with consecutive squares sharing one complete side and no square touching any nonconsecutive square along an edge. For n such squares, the total perimeter before gluing would be 4n unit edges. Each shared side is counted twice internally and is not part of the outside perimeter, so subtract 2 for every shared side. A chain of n squares has n - 1 shared sides. Therefore P = 4n - 2(n - 1) = 2n + 2. Substitute n = 2013 to get P = 2(2013) + 2 = 4028 cm.
